notable_absence.finding: This page never uses the phrase 'Service Plan' - it consistently says 'Support Plan' or 'Plan'. But it is NOT internally consistent about the top tier's full name: the section heading reads 'Enterprise Plan' (#enterprise), the credit-card-payment note reads 'Enterprise Support Plan', and the Model Service billing note reads 'Enterprise Plan pricing' / 'Enterprise [On-Demand credits]' - three different phrasings for the same tier within a single page.

cross_component_finding: Directly resolves this round's hypothesis for the billing side: 'Enterprise Support Plan' (matching one of the two previously-flagged variants) is the phrase actually used for the commercial gate (e.g. 'You must have a contract to deploy clusters and services on the Enterprise Support Plan'). 'Enterprise Service Plan' does not appear anywhere in this batch's billing pages. So the billing docs do not add a third variant - they reinforce 'Enterprise Support Plan' as (one of) the intended wording(s) - but they also introduce a new intra-page variant, plain 'Enterprise Plan', used for both the section heading and the Model Service pricing note, showing the inconsistency is broader than just 'Support' vs 'Service'.
cross_product_finding: Unlike server/, where feature availability is gated by product edition (Enterprise Edition vs Community Edition), Capella gates commercial capabilities (contract-only payment methods, technical-support SLAs of 30 minutes vs 8 hours vs forums-only) on a purchased Support Plan tier - confirming the requiresSupportPlan / requiresEdition distinction already established in the registry rather than blurring it.
